sequence_description: Direct JWT endpoint: attempt alg=none token acceptance vs a valid control token; also ensure attacker does not get a valid session/identity.
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT auth accepted an attacker token using alg=none (unsigned JWT), resulting in a valid session token and identity being issued.

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT auth accepted an attacker token using alg=none (unsigned JWT), resulting in a valid session token and identity being issued.

sequence_description: Direct JWT login: attempt kid header injection to select an attacker-controlled key (untrusted) while keeping claims semantically valid; ensure Vault rejects and does not mint a session.
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT login succeeded for the attacker-crafted token intended to exploit kid header injection (untrusted key selection), indicating the broker may be accepting tokens signed by an untrusted key or not enforcing key allowlisting by kid.

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT login succeeded for the attacker-crafted token intended to exploit kid header injection (untrusted key selection), indicating the broker may be accepting tokens signed by an untrusted key or not enforcing key allowlisting by kid.

sequence_description: Config-change + re-auth: start with trusted JWKS URL and successful control login; then switch jwks_url to an attacker JWKS while keeping bound_issuer constant and attempt to login with attacker-signed token claiming the same issuer.
description: [LLM-Judge] Trust anchor substitution: after switching jwt_validation jwks_url to an attacker-controlled JWKS while keeping the issuer binding constant, the system accepted an attacker-signed JWT for the same issuer and issued a valid session token.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Trust anchor substitution: after switching jwt_validation jwks_url to an attacker-controlled JWKS while keeping the issuer binding constant, the system accepted an attacker-signed JWT for the same issuer and issued a valid session token.

sequence_description: Re-sign attack: same semantic claims (iss/aud/sub) but signed with an untrusted key should be rejected; includes a second identity to ensure no cross-identity acceptance.
description: [LLM-Judge] JWTs re-signed with an untrusted/attacker key were accepted (signature/key trust not enforced), allowing forged authentication.

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWTs re-signed with an untrusted/attacker key were accepted (signature/key trust not enforced), allowing forged authentication.

sequence_description: Brokered-flow probe: send unsigned request object (alg=none) to an upstream OIDC authorization endpoint to test request-object signature enforcement; then repeat with a second identity to check consistent rejection.
description: [LLM-Judge] Unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none) probe did not yield an explicit accept/reject signal; both attempts resulted in HTTP 307 redirects and overall LOGIN_FAILED, making signature-enforcement behavior unclear and potentially indicative of improper error handling or redirect-based bypass conditions.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none) probe did not yield an explicit accept/reject signal; both attempts resulted in HTTP 307 redirects and overall LOGIN_FAILED, making signature-enforcement behavior unclear and potentially indicative of improper error handling or redirect-based bypass conditions.

sequence_description: Attack: Revoke a Vault session token and verify it can no longer be used (anti-replay of revoked artifacts).
description: [LLM-Judge] Session revocation failed with a server-side error ('no namespace'), preventing validation that revoked tokens are actually invalidated and suggesting a misconfiguration or broken revocation endpoint.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Session revocation failed with a server-side error ('no namespace'), preventing validation that revoked tokens are actually invalidated and suggesting a misconfiguration or broken revocation endpoint.

sequence_description: Attack: JWT with iat far in the future should be rejected when clock_skew_leeway is disabled; verify baseline acceptance with default leeway, then tighten leeway and re-auth to ensure rejection.
description: [LLM-Judge] JWTs with an iat far in the future are still accepted even after clock_skew_leeway was tightened/disabled, indicating iat future-skew validation bypass or misapplied config.

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWTs with an iat far in the future are still accepted even after clock_skew_leeway was tightened/disabled, indicating iat future-skew validation bypass or misapplied config.

sequence_description: Attack: JWT with iat far in the future should be rejected when clock_skew_leeway is disabled; verify baseline acceptance with default leeway, then tighten leeway and re-auth to ensure rejection.
description: [LLM-Judge] Role config readback shows clock_skew_leeway as null/None after modification, suggesting the tighten operation may not have taken effect or the system treats null as default permissive behavior.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Role config readback shows clock_skew_leeway as null/None after modification, suggesting the tighten operation may not have taken effect or the system treats null as default permissive behavior.

sequence_description: JWT auth configured with key-A; baseline login succeeds. Then trust is rotated to key-B and the same claims are used again (now signed by key-A). Login must be rejected to prove immediate trust-anchor propagation.
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT signing key rotation did not take effect immediately: a token signed with the old key (key-A) was still accepted after validation was reconfigured to trust key-B.

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT signing key rotation did not take effect immediately: a token signed with the old key (key-A) was still accepted after validation was reconfigured to trust key-B.

sequence_description: Case confusion attack: test whether sub='Admin' and sub='admin' collapse into the same Vault entity (case-folding/normalization bug in alias mapping).
description: [LLM-Judge] Case-variant JWT subjects ('Admin' vs 'admin') are mapped to the same canonical entity, indicating case-folding/normalization in alias mapping that can enable identity collision/impersonation.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Case-variant JWT subjects ('Admin' vs 'admin') are mapped to the same canonical entity, indicating case-folding/normalization in alias mapping that can enable identity collision/impersonation.

sequence_description: Empty-subject attack: test whether sub='' causes multiple distinct principals to collapse into a shared entity (e.g., empty alias name).
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT login with empty subject/alias fails with HTTP 500 (server error) instead of a clean client-side rejection, indicating possible unhandled input leading to DoS/error disclosure risk.

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT login with empty subject/alias fails with HTTP 500 (server error) instead of a clean client-side rejection, indicating possible unhandled input leading to DoS/error disclosure risk.

sequence_description: Identity-claim pointer confusion: baseline uses sub; then switch identity_claim to a nested JSON pointer so two distinct principals can be forced to share the same alias value.
description: [LLM-Judge] Identity alias collision: changing identity_claim to a nested JSON pointer (/user/id) allows two distinct JWT principals to be mapped to the same internal identity entity, enabling impersonation/account confusion.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Identity alias collision: changing identity_claim to a nested JSON pointer (/user/id) allows two distinct JWT principals to be mapped to the same internal identity entity, enabling impersonation/account confusion.
